name: TLV62084DSGR
title: TLV62080, TLV62084, TLV62084A 1.2 A and 2 A synchronous step-down converters, 2 mm × 2 mm WSON-8
summary: A family of small synchronous buck converters with both MOSFETs on chip, for inputs of 2.5 V or 2.7 V up to 6 V. The TLV62080 delivers 1.2 A; the TLV62084 and TLV62084A deliver 2 A. The output is set from 0.5 V to 4 V by a divider on FB against a 0.45 V reference. DCS-Control runs the part at a nominal 2 MHz in PWM and moves it into power save mode at light load; it also offers 100% duty cycle, soft start, output discharge, an open-drain power-good output, UVLO, current limit and thermal shutdown.

pins.name: EN
pins.function: Enable. A logic high starts the converter; a logic low shuts it down. It must be driven or tied, never left open.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground for both the power stage and the control circuits.

pins.name: FB
pins.function: Feedback input of the control loop. It takes the tap of the external output divider, which sets VOUT.

pins.name: VOS
pins.function: Output sense input of the control loop; it is wired to the output voltage.

pins.name: PG
pins.function: Power-good output, open drain. It pulls low while the output is under its regulation window. It may float when not needed.

pins.name: SW
pins.function: Switch node, the joined drains of the internal high-side and low-side MOSFETs. It drives the output filter inductor.

pins.name: PAD
pins.function: Exposed thermal pad. It is tied to GND and soldered down, both for heat removal and for mechanical strength.

circuits.title: Typical Application Schematic, 2.8 V to 4.2 V in, 1.2 V out
circuits.description: The TLV62084 stepping a 2.8 V to 4.2 V supply down to 1.2 V at up to 2 A. EN is tied to VIN, so the converter runs whenever the input is up. C1 (ceramic) and C3 (tantalum) bypass the input. L1 and C2 form the output filter, the 1 µH and 22 µF pairing from the filter table. VOS senses the output directly. R1 and R2 divide the output to the 0.45 V the FB pin regulates: 0.45 V × (1 + 65.3 k / 39.2 k) = 1.2 V. R3 pulls the open-drain PG output up to VOUT and gives the power-good signal.

parts.note: 2.2 A, 3 mm × 3 mm × 1.2 mm, Coilcraft XFL3012-102MEB

circuits.title: Typical Application Circuit
circuits.description: The TLV62084 with its output set by the R1/R2 divider: VOUT = 0.45 V × (1 + R1 / R2). A 10 µF capacitor bypasses VIN, and EN is tied to VIN. The 1 µH inductor and 22 µF capacitor filter the output, VOS reads it, and a 180 kΩ resistor from VOUT pulls up the open-drain PG output.

operation.text: Three versions come in the 2 mm × 2 mm WSON-8 package. TLV62080: 2.5 V to 6 V in, 1.2 A out. TLV62084: 2.7 V to 6 V in, 2 A out. TLV62084A: as the TLV62084, but its PG output is held low while the part is disabled, in UVLO or in thermal shutdown, where the other two leave PG at high impedance.

DCS-Control, a regulation scheme mixing hysteretic and voltage-mode control. Under medium and heavy load the converter runs PWM at a nominal 2 MHz, the frequency moving within a controlled range as the input changes. At light load it slides into power save mode without a step on the output. Load-transient response is fast, DC regulation tight and output ripple low. Compensation is internal and tolerates a wide range of output capacitance.

Power save mode starts once the inductor current turns discontinuous. Pulses are of fixed on time, typically ton = 400 ns × VOUT / VIN, and the switching frequency falls with load while the quiescent current is kept to a minimum.

As the input drops toward the output, the part moves into 100% duty cycle: the high-side MOSFET stays on and the low-side stays off. The output then follows the input less the drop across the high-side switch and the inductor resistance, which stretches a battery's usable range.
A logic high on EN starts switching and the output regulates to its set point; a logic low disables the part. EN has to be terminated; it must not float.
Whenever the part shuts down, through EN, thermal shutdown or UVLO, the output is discharged through SW by an internal resistor of typically RDIS (1 kΩ).

After EN goes high the part waits about 40 µs before switching, then ramps VOUT at roughly 10 mV/µs. This limits inrush and keeps high-impedance cells from sagging. If heavy load keeps the output from reaching its target within the ramp, the part carries on in normal operation with the current limit active. It starts cleanly into a pre-biased output, ramping from the voltage already present.

PG is an open-drain output specified for a typical sink current of 0.5 mA. It goes high impedance once the output passes 95% of its set value and pulls low when the output falls under typically 90%. It needs a pull-up resistor, best taken to the converter's own output. On the TLV62080 and TLV62084, PG is high impedance during disable, UVLO and thermal shutdown; on the TLV62084A it is low in those states. With VIN below 0.7 V, PG is high impedance on all three. PG can drive the EN pin of a following converter for sequencing, and can be left open when not used.
Below VUVLO (1.8 V typical, falling) the part shuts down; it restarts once the input rises by the hysteresis, 120 mV typical.
The part stops at a junction temperature of typically TJSD (150 °C) and resumes on its own once the junction has cooled by the 20 °C hysteresis.

Current is sensed in both the high-side and the low-side MOSFET. When the high-side limit trips, the high side turns off and the low side turns on until the current has fallen to the low-side limit; then the high side turns on again. This repeats for as long as the current keeps reaching the high-side limit. It guards against a shorted or saturated inductor, an overload or a shorted output. Propagation delay makes the actual peak current higher than the static ILIM figure.
Input 2.5 V (TLV62080) or 2.7 V (TLV62084, TLV62084A) up to 6 V; output current up to 1.2 A (TLV62080) or 2 A (TLV62084, TLV62084A).

L and COUT together form the output low-pass filter. Recommended pairings are 1 µH or 2.2 µH with 10 µF to 100 µF; the typical application uses 1 µH with 22 µF. A larger inductance lowers ripple current but slows the transient response. Output capacitance from 10 µF to 100 µF and more is supported; with large values, stability is confirmed by a load-transient test or a measured Bode plot.

On the input, a low-ESR ceramic serves as the converter's low-impedance source, sitting across VIN and GND right at those pins. 10 µF serves most designs; more reduces input ripple current. On the output, small low-ESR ceramics give low ripple; X5R or X7R dielectric holds the capacitance at high frequency and across temperature.
For accuracy R2 stays under 40 kΩ, so the divider current is at least 100 times IFB. A lower total divider resistance is more immune to injected noise; a higher one draws less current.
The source feeding VIN is rated for the current the converter draws at its input voltage, output voltage and load.

Input capacitor, output capacitor and inductor sit as close to the IC as possible, on short, wide, direct traces to keep resistance and parasitic inductance low. Use one common power ground; both capacitors' ground terminals join it directly, so the ground potential does not shift. FB and VOS are signal traces and are kept away from the SW node. Ground layers may be used for shielding. The suggested placement puts C1 beside VIN and GND, L1 on SW, C2 at the output, and R1 and R2 next to FB.

The power the part can dissipate in a small surface-mount package depends on the system: thermal coupling, airflow, heat sinks and other heat sources nearby. Thermal performance improves with a board designed to spread heat, with the thermal pad soldered down, and with airflow.
